name: Question 16
problem: Every week at a restaurant $2$ out of $100$ plates, on average, get a little breakage and are replaced at the end of the week. If the manager is checking the plates at the end of a certain week, what is the probability that they will check more than $4$ plates before finding a broken one? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of plates checked until a broken one is found. On average, the chance of finding a broken plate is 

$$
p=\frac{2}{100}=0.02.
$$

So, the number of plates that the manager checks before finding a broken one can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.02.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.02).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.02)^{x-1}(0.02) \\  & =(0.98)^{x-1}(0.02)\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X>4),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>4)=1-P(X\le 4)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 4) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.98)^{1-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{2-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{3-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{4-1}(0.02) \\  & =(0.02)+(0.98)(0.02)+(0.98)^{2}(0.02)+(0.98)^{3}(0.02) \\  & =[1+0.98+(0.98)^{2}+(0.98)^{3}](0.02) \\  & ≈0.078\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of checking more than $4$ plates before finding a broken one is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>4) & =1-P(X\le 4) \\  & ≈1-0.078 \\  & =0.922\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Question 16

Every week at a restaurant 2 out of 100 plates, on average, get a little breakage and are replaced at the end of the week. If the manager is checking the plates at the end of a certain week, what is the probability that they will check more than 4 plates before finding a broken one? Round your answer to 3 decimal places.

a
0.922
b
0.999
c
0.884
d
0.078
e
0.001
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A geometric random variable X with probability of success p has the following probability mass function:

f(x)=(1−p)x−1p

Let X be the number of plates checked until a broken one is found. On average, the chance of finding a broken plate is p=2100=0.02.

So, the number of plates that the manager checks before finding a broken one can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success p=0.02.

So, X∼Geom(0.02). In this case, X has the following probability mass function:

f(x)=(1−0.02)x−1(0.02)=(0.98)x−1(0.02)

To compute P(X>4), we will use the complement:

P(X>4)=1−P(X≤4)

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

P(X≤4)=P(X∈{1,2,3,4})=f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)=(0.98)1−1(0.02)+(0.98)2−1(0.02)+(0.98)3−1(0.02)+(0.98)4−1(0.02)=(0.02)+(0.98)(0.02)+(0.98)2(0.02)+(0.98)3(0.02)=[1+0.98+(0.98)2+(0.98)3](0.02)≈0.078

rounded to 3 decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of checking more than 4 plates before finding a broken one is

P(X>4)=1−P(X≤4)≈1−0.078=0.922

rounded to 3 decimal places.
